subject: FY21 Budget Departmental Reviews and Staffing Priorities
overview: The School Committee reviewed fiscal year 2021 budget requests for the art, physical education, library media, health services, and athletics departments. The committee discussed equipment replacement cycles, the district’s transition to remote learning technology, and the process for prioritizing new personnel requests under projected financial constraints.

items.title: Fine Arts Budget
items.summary: Director Tony Szykniej presented a level-funded budget request that prioritized piano tuning, marching band transportation, and the ongoing replacement of deteriorating art room stools.

items.title: Physical Education and Health Budget
items.summary: Director Rachel Perry requested two new full-time positions for adaptive physical education and middle school health to meet inclusivity goals and state mandates.

items.title: Library Media and Technology Budget
items.summary: Director Molly Laden highlighted the district's recent acquisition of 1,000 Chromebooks but noted the need for a large-scale capital replacement of over 1,200 aging desktop computers from 2012.

items.title: Budget Prioritization and Staffing Discussion
items.summary: The committee debated the exclusion of new personnel requests from the baseline budget and the impact of the COVID-19 pandemic on the city’s ability to fund a projected 5% increase.

items.title: Health Services Budget
items.summary: Director Toni Wray requested an increase for medical supplies and summer stipends, while identifying the need for full-time nursing coverage at Curtis Tufts High School and Andrews Middle School.

items.title: Athletics Budget
items.summary: Director Robert Maloney reviewed the athletics budget, noting that middle school sports programs were successfully operating within current funding levels.

items.title: Revolving Accounts Financial Review
items.summary: The committee discussed the transparency of revolving accounts for community schools and food services. Approved a motion to conduct a detailed financial review of all significant revolving accounts by October 15.
